acceptance: Review real captures at 320×568, 390×844, 768×1024, 1023×900, 1440×900 and 1920×1080. This specification is approval to build, not approval of the finished screen.

The scope is the public business chapter, its Loyalty sequence and the overlays opened from that sequence. Preserve the as-built V2 hero, earning chapters, marketplace demonstration, Monthly Content and footer. Do not invent replacement homepage content.

The phone homepage first screen contains fewer than 40 visible words, including navigation. The Loyalty stage has a hard ceiling of 29 simultaneously visible words, including controls, data, truth labels and legible lettering inside media. Count the actual capture, not just authored headings.

Only the active animated scene is rendered visually. Do not place eight hidden-but-readable scenes behind the active scene. Report the complete expanded copy separately for reduced-motion stills and disclosures.

The initial Story scene has 12 authored visible words, leaving 17 for intrinsic asset lettering. Verify the supplied creative before claiming the word target passes. If it exceeds that allowance, stop for art-direction review; do not crop its lettering, shrink it into illegibility or substitute another business.
Get attention, signup, a distinct member QR, dated counted visits and Reward ready are understandable without opening any disclosure.
The same From Jasmine source line remains stationary throughout the sequence. It never migrates into the Wallet card or becomes a claim of verified sales.
The public replay cannot change the business provider. Opening either business preview still shows the baseline ten-member fixture, including Sara at four visits.
No signup, visit, Wallet save, redemption, campaign click or notification event is written by playback, scrubbing, scrolling or viewing an image.
A member QR decodes correctly, has a four-module quiet zone and remains at least 144px square. No acquisition QR is substituted for it.
No simulated operating-system sheet, notification banner, cursor-driven consent, delivery receipt, money counter or automatic redemption appears.

Test keyboard operation, screen-reader scene descriptions, 200% text zoom, touch scrubbing, browser Back, reduced motion and failed media loading. There must be no horizontal page overflow or inaccessible scene content.
spec.signature_moment: A film-style scrubber follows one fictional member through time while From Jasmine stays fixed outside every object. No live loyalty product or Wallet card should expose a control that rewinds someone’s visits; here it is explicitly a public replay. The last cut reveals the business’s reward receipt, not a pretend device notification.

honest_states: Initial rest: the Story is a still image. Nothing plays or records a campaign click on page load.

The signup scene is a read-only editorial excerpt of Sara’s historical demo signup. It is not a functioning form and does not depict automatic consent. Full terms and the operative agreement belong to the working signup route, not this abbreviated public replay.
Signup produces zero visits in the replay. Its first visit is a separate, date-labelled scene.
The September 10 return is on a different America/Chicago business day. September 13 and September 16 are separate cuts, not digits counted up by a timer.
September 17 is an explicitly fictional continuation from the baseline. It earns a reward but never redeems it.
The final receipt says Wallet update · simulated. It does not claim a device changed, a notification was delivered or a pass was saved.
The public card uses a supported subset of Apple store-card fields. It is not a tiny screenshot of the complete business card and does not alter the full card specification on the working routes.
Unknown or failed media remains labelled absence. No Demo Roastery asset, Jasmine portrait or generated interface is substituted.
The source disclosure explains that the working business demo remains unchanged. Replay, route navigation and Back do not reset or mutate the business’s in-memory scenario.
Get started opens an honest Lab handoff, not authentication, account creation or a simulated production success.
spec.two_second_read: A creator brings someone in. The same source stays attached while visits become a reward. Open the working business preview next.
media: Retained acquisition demonstration: preserve /uploads/seed/tapmart-recreate.jpg, /uploads/seed/tapmart-story.jpg and /uploads/seed/tapmart-car.jpg in their existing V2 public placements. Recreate and the photographed Story phone remain intact 4:5 images; the car may use the approved 3:2 crop at 50% 68%. These are campaign imagery, not Jasmine or Loopday fixture evidence. Do not reuse them as the Loyalty source.

Loyalty source: /design-lab/story-loopday-01.jpg, verified as the matched Loopday 9:16 creative. Show the complete asset without a phone bezel, perspective extraction, overlay copy or play symbol on the image. Phone display 246×437px at 390; 234×416px at 320; desktop 300×533px. Reserve dimensions. Transcribe and count intrinsic lettering during media-manifest review; do not claim inspection from this specification.

Wallet artwork: /design-lab/reference-loopday-01.jpg. In a 375:123 strip, reserve the left 62% as solid #18231D for the primary field and place the photograph in the right 38%, object-fit cover. Start at object-position 50% 50%, then verify and record a subject-safe crop. No gradient, face removal, global grade or invented logo overlay.

Coded Loopday mark: 40×40 view box; a 3px open circular stroke centered at 20,20 with radius 13 and a 40-degree opening toward the lower right. The final 7px tangent is brick #B73E28; the remainder is paper on ink. Render at 28px on the pass and 40px on the signup excerpt. It is a brand mark, not a stamp or progress indicator.

Coded public Apple store-card concept: 375px reference width and approximately 500px content-led height, 12px outer radius, flat #18231D, paper values and #C4CDBF labels. Header contains the loop mark and Loopday Coffee. Primary field is VISITS with the full value. Two lower supported fields show the reward value Free coffee with no redundant label, and STATUS with Collecting or Reward ready. A black-on-white member QR occupies the lower area. This public field selection intentionally omits the MEMBER field and visible member ID; neither is essential to the public decision. The full working card retains them. No custom strokes, buttons, source attribution or notification UI are printed on the pass.

Public pass sizing: 358px wide at 390, 296px at 320, 375px on tablet and desktop. Preserve 16px minimum field text, 13px labels and a 32px primary value rather than scaling the entire DOM. Header padding 20px, field-group gaps 20px, QR white square 184px at 390 and 160px at 320. Let height grow at text zoom.

Coded member QR: generate a real QR at error correction M from the opaque fixture payload tapmart-demo-member:loopday:q7n4k9r2m6t8. Use black square modules, integer raster alignment or crisp vector paths, four white modules of quiet zone on every side and no logo. This is the same token in all historical scenes, contains no contact or source information, and performs no action when displayed. It is not a URL, signup QR or real Wallet credential.

Coded signup excerpt: square-edged paper surface, loop mark, business, reward and fixed rule followed by two read-only field representations and a depicted ink action. Use real text and layout, not a screenshot. It is an editorial selection from the actual signup, not a separate shortened signup implementation.

Coded final business receipt: open paper working band, not a Wallet pass or notification toast. Sara sits above five equal progress strokes, then 5 of 5 visits, Reward ready, Free coffee and Wallet update · simulated. Five strokes are 4px high with 8px gaps; all are ink after the final depicted event. No enclosing status card, green glow or celebration.

Coded acquisition seam: one straight 2px #C4CDBF line attached to the outside source label, with a 12px brick terminal. On desktop it connects the stable source datum to the current object boundary. On phone it is a short horizontal rule above the scene. It is a relationship cue, never a metric or progress bar.
